question: How do Health Canada and the Canadian Food Inspection Agency divide responsibility for food labelling in Canada?
generated_answer:
Health Canada is responsible for setting policies and standards for the safety and nutritional quality of all food sold in Canada. You can find out more about Health Canada's role in food safety at Food Safety and Nutrition. The Canadian Food Inspection Agency (CFIA) is responsible for the administration of food labelling legislation and regulations for food sold in Canada. The CFIA also enforces the legislation and regulations governing the safety and nutritional quality of food sold in Canada. You can find out more about the CFIA's role in food labelling at Food Labelling and Nutrition. 2. What is the purpose of food labelling in Canada? The purpose of food labelling in Canada is to help Canadians make informed food choices. Food labels provide information that can help you choose nutritious foods and avoid exposure to certain chemicals or allergens. 3. What information must be included on food labels in Canada? In Canada, food labels must include the following information:

- The name of the food

- The net quantity of the food

- The ingredients of the food

- The nutritional information of the food

- Any allergens or other substances that may cause adverse reactions

- Any other information required by law

4. How do I know if a food label is accurate? In Canada, food labels are subject to strict regulations and standards. The CFIA enforces these regulations and standards to ensure that food labels are accurate and truthful. If you have concerns about the accuracy of a food label, you can contact the CFIA for more information. 5. What are the consequences of mislabeling food in Canada? In Canada, mislabeling food is a serious offence. The CFIA takes mislabeling very seriously and can impose fines and other penalties on individuals or companies that mislabel food. In some cases, mislabeling can also lead to food recalls and other safety measures. 6. How can I report a suspected case of mislabeling food in Canada? If you suspect that a food label is inaccurate or misleading, you can report it to the CFIA. You can contact the CFIA by phone, email, or online. The CFIA will investigate your report and take appropriate action if necessary. 7. What are the benefits of accurate food labelling in Canada? Accurate food labelling in Canada has many benefits, including:

- Helping Canadians make informed food choices

- Reducing the risk of foodborne illness and other health problems

- Promoting transparency and accountability in the food industry

- Supporting the development of a safe and nutritious food supply

8. How can I get more information about food labelling in Canada? If you have questions about food labelling in Canada, you can contact the CFIA for more information. The CFIA has a wealth of resources and information available on its website, including fact sheets, guides, and other materials. You can also contact the CFIA by phone, email, or online.
